To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
anti-consumption discourse can produce two consumer-resistant identities: a hero resistant identity and a project resistant identity.
the voluntary simplicity discourse and culture jamming discourse, two dominant anti-consumer discourses, produce two consumer-resistant identities: hero identities and project identities.
anti-consumption discourse and consumer resistant identity are important in the construction of anti-consumptive practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of consumer identities and the role of anti-consumptive discourses in the formation of consumer identities.
the development of a new consumer identity that is resistant to consumer culture and that is based on anti-consumption values.
the question of why people resist consumption and what they gain from this resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anti-consumption movement is not a movement at all, but an array of different movements, each with different motivations, different strategies, and different goals.
anti-consumption is a central part of consumer culture, and that anti-consumers can be seen as a new type of consumer.
consumer resistance can be a powerful tool for consumer empowerment, but that it should not be considered as a universal solution to the problems of consumerism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the consumer resistance literature is in need of an identity turn.
the study of anti-consumers is not only about the understanding of the reasons why people resist consumption but also about the understanding of how they resist consumption.
the consumer-resistant identities are the result of a process of identity formation that is based on a dialectical relation between the individual and the social context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumer resistance is a dynamic process that is shaped and reshaped by consumers’ identities.
consumer identities can be understood in terms of resistance to consumer culture and that these resistant identities can be expressed in terms of political and creative consumption.
consumer resistance is more complex than a simple reaction against the dominant culture.
